A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mol-LLaMA study. Their main texts, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original general-understanding evaluations, PAMPA and BBBP prediction results, encoder and dataset ablations, and qualitative molecular analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Mol-LLaMA results on MoleculeQA, Mol-Instructions task transfer, and 3D-MoIT computed-property questions. Attribution of some baseline scores to prior papers does not affect this assessment.

M1.justification: Both versions use MoleculeSTM and UniMol encoders, the same cross-attention blending module, SciBERT-initialized Q-Former, and Llama backbones. The three instruction-data types, filtering procedure, representation-learning objectives, and LoRA instruction tuning are retained. Additional benchmark fine-tuning does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v3 adds factual molecular question answering on MoleculeQA, captioning and property prediction from Mol-Instructions, and basic and quantum-property questions from 3D-MoIT (Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3). This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained PubChem explanations and PAMPA/BBBP permeability tasks.

E2.justification: New reported comparisons include MolT5, BioT5, MoMu, MolCA, and BioMedGPT-LM on MoleculeQA; Alpaca, Baize, and Vicuna on task transfer; and Uni-Mol and 2D-MoLM on computed-property questions. Many baseline scores are explicitly imported from prior papers. Tables 10–11 also add GPT-4o, LLaMo, and 3D-MoLM responses to previously Mol-LLaMA-only case studies.

E3.justification: v3 adds task-specific fine-tuning evaluations alongside the retained zero-shot tests. MoleculeQA uses 20 epochs, batch size 256, learning rate 1e-4, and greedy decoding (Appendix C.3); other new tasks introduce captioning metrics, MAE, and valid-response rates. The BBBP table also changes Mol-Instructions' stated backbone from Llama3.1-8B to Llama3-8B, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The quantitative ablations and existing PAMPA response analyses are retained. v3 adds a diphenyl-ether case contrasting single encoders, concatenation, and blending (Table 7), expands the Nystatin and adenosine comparisons, and adds Mol-Instructions' SELFIES-producing PAMPA responses. These are focused additions to the existing analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages from three GPT-4o evaluations for general-understanding scores. Neither introduces seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional valid-response percentages are performance metrics, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched general-understanding, PAMPA, BBBP, and quantitative ablation scores are unchanged. v3 adds substantial results, including MoleculeQA totals of 67.97 and 70.76 for the two Mol-LLaMA backbones, Mol-Instructions property-prediction MAEs of 0.0035 and 0.0039, and eight computed-property results per backbone (Tables 5 and 12–14). These are new evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.1 formally defines the multimodal training variables and negative log-likelihood objective in Equation 1. v3 omits this formal preliminary section and equation while retaining the described training approach. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain general molecular understanding through three instruction-data types and complementary 2D–3D blending, enabling informative responses with explanations. Reasoning and rationale generation were already claimed in v1. Their greater prominence and additional supporting benchmarks in v3 do not materially redefine the core claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit analysis-only limitation and defers molecule generation through a reward-model framework to future work (Appendix D). It also interprets transfer results and distinguishes missing structural components from incorrect connectivity in the new blending case study. The existing BBBP qualification about external knowledge is retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds the exact general-response judging prompt, PAMPA conformer-generation tools, predefined TDC splitting and greedy-decoding details, MoleculeQA hyperparameters, and a project-page pointer. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the original experiments. Conversely, v1's explicit attribution of the 100-molecule evaluation's PubChem test split is no longer stated.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to MoleculeQA, BioMedGPT, BioT5, and Yue et al. on reasoning, including a new BioMedGPT discussion. Several references associated with the removed baseline-description subsection disappear. The principal positioning against task-specific molecular assistants remains consistent.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and dataset motivation are extensively rewritten around two challenges. v3 removes the preliminary and standalone baseline subsections, brings the leading case study into the introduction, reverses the ablation discussion order, and consolidates formerly separated appendix results. This substantially changes the narrative and organization.

P2.justification: v3 switches the main text from two columns to one and substantially restructures response and example tables. It merges the earlier Bromazepam appendix tables, splits instruction examples across three tables, reverses ablation panels, and adds benchmark, diagnostic, and judging-prompt displays. Existing architecture diagrams are retained despite relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v1's evidence centered on GPT-4o-rated explanations and two permeability tasks. v3 substantially strengthens empirical support through factual-answer accuracy and captioning/basic/quantum-property evaluations (Tables 5 and 12–14), reducing dependence on that narrow evaluation base. Added protocol documentation and explicit applicability limits also improve assessability. The new fine-tuned results support task transfer rather than stronger zero-shot reliability, but the overall evidential gain is substantial.
